description:
You are an urban economist at the San Francisco Controller's Office. The Board of Supervisors has requested a 5-year housing shortage projection to support pending zoning reform legislation. You must quantify how many net new housing units the city can realistically produce each year compared to expected household growth — and document the cumulative shortfall.

Using the UrbanSim orca framework and the San Francisco dataset at /home/ga/urbansim_projects/data/sanfran_public.h5, build and execute a 5-year (2020–2024) annual housing simulation. Your simulation must track both demand and supply:

- Demand side: Model annual household growth. Use a growth rate derived from the existing data or standard Bay Area projections (e.g., 1–2% per year).
- Supply side: Model annual housing production. Estimate new units that can realistically be built each year from underdeveloped parcels — parcels where current building density is significantly below the maximum allowed by zoning. Apply a development probability (what fraction of feasible parcels actually develop in any given year) based on historical SF development rates.

The simulation must use orca.run() with iter_vars listing each year, with at least a demand_growth step and a housing_supply step registered via @orca.step(). At each simulated year, the steps must update the orca tables and log the year's outcomes.

After the simulation completes, produce:
- /home/ga/urbansim_projects/output/housing_shortage.csv — 5 rows (one per year), with columns: year, households_start, new_households, new_units, annual_deficit, cumulative_deficit
- /home/ga/urbansim_projects/output/shortage_trend.png — dual-axis or overlaid line chart showing new_households and new_units per year, with annual_deficit highlighted

The analysis must run in /home/ga/urbansim_projects/notebooks/housing_shortage.ipynb using the UrbanSim (Python 3) kernel. Jupyter Lab is open at http://localhost:8888.
